ask: Lane 6 of the premises brief; its full text is in the Ask of c7 (fix the reply-style conflict). Plan: plans/premise-handoffs-plan.md in the project files.
note: Planners already run on Opus with a fresh context per lane, so model and context are not the gap. The gap: a planner plans inside its brief and never doubts it, sees one lane only, and reads a repo that lacks your newest rulings (o5b). Shape, advisor pick Oct 21, not yet ruled: no new reviewer. The planner prompt gains one duty: before planning, list the premises the brief rests on, each with its source ('from notes' or 'measured in run X'), check each against decisions/ and recent rulings, and name any that don't hold and any simpler route. The orchestrator does the same check once, across lanes, when it writes a batch's briefs. Three layers together steer: rulings filed the day they're made (o5b), the question judge (c7), this premise check. Draft with c7. Goal session report, Oct 22: built and reviewed, waiting for the next batch (batch 6).
title: Planners check their brief's premises before planning
why: Your question, Oct 21: can questions steer the work? A question judge (c7) only acts when a session stops to ask; a wrong premise in a plan can reach a PR without ever becoming a question. Today's 'the freeze stops me' was baked into the plan.
